title: Toward Human-Centered AI-Assisted Terminology Work
abstract: arXiv:2512.18859v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Generative AI is likely to transform terminology work by creating new opportunities for automation. At the same time, it raises concerns about the future of terminologists and terminological resources, as efficiency pressures may encourage excessive automation based on the perception that human expertise can be replaced by AI. However, large language models remain unreliable for terminological purposes due to errors, hallucinations, and various forms of bias, making terminologists indispensable for ensuring the accuracy and reliability of terminological data. This paper argues that human-centered AI, an approach that emphasizes that AI's primary goal should be to contribute to human well-being, provides a framework for maximizing the benefits of generative AI while mitigating its risks. translated_title: 迈向以人为中心的AI辅助术语工作
translated_abstract: 生成式AI很可能通过创造新的自动化机会来变革术语工作。与此同时，它也引发了对术语学家和术语资源未来的担忧，因为效率压力可能促使人们基于“人类专业知识可以被AI取代”的认知而走向过度自动化。然而，由于错误、幻觉和各种形式的偏见，大型语言模型在术语学应用中仍然不可靠，这使得术语学家在确保术语数据的准确性和可靠性方面不可或缺。本文认为，以人为中心的AI——一种强调AI的首要目标应是促进人类福祉的方法——为在最大化生成式AI益处的同时减轻其风险提供了一个框架。文章主张，高水平的自动化与有意义的人类控制是兼容且值得追求的，AI应当增强术语学家的能力，而非取代他们。
tldr: 本文提出应以“以人为中心的AI”框架指导术语工作，在实现高水平自动化的同时保留有意义的人类控制，因为大型语言模型存在错误、幻觉和偏见，术语学家对确保术语数据的准确可靠仍然不可或缺。
en_tdlr: This paper argues that terminology work should adopt a human-centered AI framework that combines high automation with meaningful human control, since large language models remain unreliable due to errors, hallucinations, and bias, making terminologists indispensable for ensuring terminological data accuracy.
